title: Trump: Ghislaine Maxwell says Jeffrey Epstein recorded Trump with his victims
description_short: Trump: Ghislaine Maxwell says Jeffrey Epstein recorded Trump with his victims
description_medium: Former 60 Minutes producer Ira Rosen wrote that Ghislaine Maxwell told him in early 2016 that Jeffrey Epstein had tapes of Donald Trump and Bill Clinton, but she did not know where they were. Rosen recounted the exchange in his 2021 memoir. No recording or independent corroboration is identified.
description_long: In his 2021 memoir, Ticking Clock, former 60 Minutes producer Ira Rosen recalled asking Ghislaine Maxwell in early 2016 whether Jeffrey Epstein had made recordings. Rosen wrote that Maxwell said Epstein had tapes of Donald Trump and Bill Clinton but that she did not know where he kept them. This is Rosen’s account of a conversation, published years after it allegedly occurred; the supplied sources do not include a recording of Maxwell’s statement or another witness who corroborated it. The claim also does not establish that any tapes existed, what they showed, or whether they included victims. Separate accounts of surveillance cameras at Epstein’s homes do not identify footage of Trump or Clinton and cannot verify Rosen’s recollection. The event can therefore be reported as a claim in Rosen’s memoir, not as proof that Epstein recorded Trump with victims. The timeline date is also approximate: the supplied account places the conversation in early 2016, while the record date is March 1.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Ghislaine Maxwell says Jeffrey Epstein recorded Trump with his victims
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Ghislaine Maxwell says Jeffrey Epstein recorded Trump with his victims

notes: The supplied current draft supports only Rosen’s 2021 recollection of a 2016 conversation. It does not establish that recordings existed, what they contained, or that Trump was recorded with victims. Proposed correction: attribute the entry to Rosen’s memoir, remove any claim of verified tapes, and correct the date to the documented memoir publication or mark the conversation date approximate.

title: Donald Trump breaks the law asking Russia to find more Clinton emails
description_short: Donald Trump breaks the law asking Russia to find more Clinton emails
description_medium: At a July 27, 2016 campaign news conference, Donald Trump publicly asked Russia to find emails Hillary Clinton had deleted from her private server. “Russia, if you’re listening, I hope you’re able to find the 30,000 emails that are missing,” he said. The quote documents a public appeal; the supplied record gives no legal finding that it violated a specific law.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump breaks the law asking Russia to find more Clinton emails
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump breaks the law asking Russia to find more Clinton emails

notes: The supplied synopsis supports the public request and quotation, but provides no legal authority or finding establishing the title’s claim that the request broke a specific law. Proposed correction: retitle as Trump’s public appeal to Russia for Clinton’s emails unless a cited legal analysis or court finding supports the claim that it broke the law.

title: Trump: WikiLeaks releases a final batch of 8,000 DNC emails
description_short: Trump: WikiLeaks releases a final batch of 8,000 DNC emails
description_medium: WikiLeaks released more than 8,000 Democratic National Committee emails late on November 6, 2016, the day before the presidential election. The files included internal campaign material, including a message listing possible Republican vice-presidential candidates. U.S. intelligence agencies later attributed the DNC hack to Russian actors; the supplied record does not show Trump directed the release.
description_long: WikiLeaks published a final batch of more than 8,000 Democratic National Committee emails late on November 6, 2016, the eve of the presidential election. The material included internal correspondence, such as a message from DNC press representative Lauren Dillon listing potential Republican vice-presidential candidates. The release followed earlier disclosures of DNC emails during the campaign. U.S. intelligence agencies later attributed the hack of DNC materials to Russian actors, while WikiLeaks was the publisher of the documents. The files entered the public debate at a politically sensitive point, but the supplied account does not establish who directed the release or show that Donald Trump coordinated with WikiLeaks or the hackers. It also does not identify how the final batch differed from preceding releases beyond its size and one example of internal material. The event is a documented publication of hacked party communications, with a later U.S. intelligence assessment about the source of the hack; it should not be described as Trump’s own action without evidence of a direct role.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: WikiLeaks releases a final batch of 8,000 DNC emails
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: WikiLeaks releases a final batch of 8,000 DNC emails

notes: The supplied account supports the publication and later intelligence attribution for the DNC hack but does not connect Trump to the release. Proposed correction: remove the Trump prefix or supply evidence of a direct role; distinguish the publisher from the actors U.S. intelligence later attributed with the hack.

title: Trump refuses to act on Russia sanctions passed by Congress
description_short: Trump refuses to act on Russia sanctions passed by Congress
description_medium: In January 2018, the Trump administration said it would not impose new sanctions under a 2017 law targeting Russia’s defense and intelligence sectors. The law authorized sanctions against people and entities doing significant business with those sectors. The supplied account does not give the administration’s stated rationale, which entities it reviewed or the scope of any sanctions already in place.
topic_tags: Countering America’s Adversaries Through Sanctions Act

preserved_fields.title: Trump refuses to act on Russia sanctions passed by Congress
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump refuses to act on Russia sanctions passed by Congress

notes: The linked timeline page returned no readable article text. The supplied material identifies the decision not to impose new sanctions but does not give the administration’s stated rationale, entities reviewed, or the scope of existing sanctions. Proposed correction: cite the official determination and distinguish a decision not to designate additional entities from failure to enforce every provision of the law.

title: Trump: Jeffrey Epstein asks journalist to write his biography
description_short: Trump: Jeffrey Epstein asks journalist to write his biography
description_medium: In early 2019, Jeffrey Epstein called journalist James B. Stewart, whom he had met the previous year, and asked whether Stewart would write his biography. Stewart later recalled that Epstein sounded “almost plaintive.” The supplied excerpt does not give the exact date or the rest of the conversation, and it does not connect the request to Donald Trump.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Jeffrey Epstein asks journalist to write his biography
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Jeffrey Epstein asks journalist to write his biography

notes: The linked TrumpFile page returned HTTP 202, and the excerpt supports only Epstein’s request to Stewart, not the rest of the exchange. No supplied source connects the call to Donald Trump. Proposed correction: remove the Trump prefix or provide a documented Trump-related link; use the memoir/article publication date if the exact call date cannot be established.
